items.rationale: The result is added after call 2, so it is in the input of calls 3, 4, 5 and 6: four calls. Each call re-sends the whole history, which is why a large tool result is paid for repeatedly. Answering 1 treats the model as reading it once; 5 or 6 miscounts which calls come after the result.

The model keeps nothing between calls or sessions. A new chat starts with a fresh context, so Monday is available only if the program saved it and loaded it back. Fading memory (a) assumes the model remembers by default; a window that is too small (c) confuses within-session capacity with storage across sessions; and (d) assumes models learn from individual chats.

An exact code such as E-47 is a precise string, which keyword search (such as BM25) matches reliably; embeddings, which capture meaning, can miss exact identifiers. Answering from the model's memory risks a confident wrong answer because the model does not hold this manual.

items.answer: Putting everything in every request would not fit or would cost far more on every call, and a crowded context makes the model recall less accurately; retrieving a few relevant pages keeps the context small and focused.
accepted: It is cheaper and more accurate: all the manuals would exceed the window or cost a lot each call, and too much context hurts the model's recall.
Too many tokens: it costs more on every call and the model gets worse at using a huge context, so only the relevant pages should go in.
items.rationale: Full credit names at least one real reason (it will not fit, or it costs more per call, or accuracy drops as the context grows); two reasons is better. Saying only that the model cannot read manuals, or that retrieval is faster, is partial or wrong.

items.answer: Summarise the conversation so far (compaction) and start a new context with the summary, or save notes outside the window and reload them as needed.
accepted: Summarise the history and continue in a fresh context
Write notes to storage and read them back later
Hand part of the task to a sub-agent with its own clean context that returns a short summary
items.rationale: Any of compaction (summarise and restart with the summary), structured notes saved outside the window, or a sub-agent with a clean context is correct. Answering that the model should just keep going, or that a bigger window is the only fix, does not address how to carry the important points forward.
